## If short on time

Keep every demo; shorten the teaching before it. Cut labs to a paired discussion of the lab question rather than dropping them. Never cut the close.

## What can go wrong

- **A demo fails on the day** — you ran `run_all.py` last week, so it is the environment: `pip install -r requirements.txt`, then re-run. Screenshots of each output live in nobody's folder: take them after your dry run.
- **No projector / terminal too small** — open `/demos` in a browser and run the same demo from the *Course labs* section.
- **The room has no laptops** — run labs as table discussions using the printed exercise sheet; you run the script and change the inputs they call out.
